<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a7199ef9744edf0c3ef0e381bb95a328545a3da9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `52d278f73411c764dacc0708876b42c422b786cd` — the merge of head `1eeab8089f223dd08909f385a79ff4c1b0e8f992` into base `a7199ef9744edf0c3ef0e381bb95a328545a3da9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 52d278f73411c764dacc0708876b42c422b786cd && git checkout 52d278f73411c764dacc0708876b42c422b786cd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a7199ef9744edf0c3ef0e381bb95a328545a3da9 1eeab8089f223dd08909f385a79ff4c1b0e8f992 && git checkout -B drift-repro a7199ef9744edf0c3ef0e381bb95a328545a3da9 && git merge --no-ff 1eeab8089f223dd08909f385a79ff4c1b0e8f992

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a7199ef9744edf0c3ef0e381bb95a328545a3da9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a7199ef9744edf0c3ef0e381bb95a328545a3da9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1eeab8089f223dd08909f385a79ff4c1b0e8f992`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-24707-introspect-pg-multischema.test.ts, .changeset/24707-pg-multischema-introspect.md + packages/services/service-datasource/src/external-datasource-service.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-service.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/default-datasource-driver-factory.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/plugin.ts, packages/rest/src/external-datasource-routes.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/runtime/src/external-validation-plugin.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sqlite-wasm/src/sqlite-wasm-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/live-dialect-matrix.testkit.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-11201-introspect-fk-schema-scope.test.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/tsconfig.json, packages/cli/src/utils/unmanaged-tables.ts, packages/spec/src/data/driver/postgres.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts, .github/workflows/ci.yml, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, knex 3.3.0 lib/dialects/postgres/query/pg-querycompiler.js (upstream, at the version pnpm-lock.yaml pins)

Inputs: card #24707 body and all four comments (triage 6282275557, claim 6292170810, dispatch 6292244225, os-dev-report 6293456848 read as claims); #11201 body and comments; PR #24920 body, file list (3 files, +271/−11) and `git diff a8b44d4070..1eeab8089f` (merge base `a8b44d4070`); the check-runs on the head. Head repo equals base repo (not a fork). Check-runs at first read 2026-10-20T15:02Z: Test Core (2/6) and (4/6) in progress; re-read 2026-10-20T15:16Z: all 41 runs completed, every conclusion `success` or `skipped`, none running. Skipped by design on a pull_request event: `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, Console Pin Gate, Build Docs, the Dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, 18.x upgrade harness, Packed-tarball smoke. Green: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · CI release & engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Test Core 1-6, Build Core, the three claim/branch guards, PR Size.

### ① Derived judgments

**The refusal's reach — right.** The only new refusal is in the PostgreSQL arm of `SqlDriver.introspectSchema` (sql-driver.ts head 15497-15536): the listing now selects `table_schema` and `array_position(current_schemas(false), table_schema::name)`, groups rows by bare `table_name`, and when any name has two or more rows it throws `postgresTableNameCollisionError` (module-private, not exported; head 4879-4895) with `code = StandardErrorCode.enum.RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, `status = 409`, BEFORE any column or key read. MySQL (`DATABASE()`) and SQLite arms are untouched, so no other dialect can meet it; `schemaByTable` stays empty there and `introspectColumns` receives `undefined`.

Who reaches `introspectSchema` in the tree at this head (`git grep`, every non-test caller): `ObjectQL.introspectDatasource` (engine.ts 21513-21522, pure delegation, throws pass through); `service-datasource/plugin.ts:94-99` wiring `config.introspect`; `ExternalDatasourceService.listRemoteTables` (external-datasource-service.ts 511-519 — the primary datasource is refused by `primaryDatasourceNotFederatedError` before any introspection), `testConnection` (582-603), `generateObjectDraft` (614), `refreshCatalog` (763), `validateObject` / `validateAll` / `validateEach` via `sweepScopedIntrospect` (814, 952, 997-1025); the datasource admin plugin's `probe` (datasource-admin-plugin.ts 871-873, `ping` → `checkHealth` → `introspectSchema` as last fallback — `SqlDriver` has `checkHealth` at head 7313, so the fallback never reaches `introspectSchema` for this driver); `TursoDriver.introspectSchema` override (turso-driver.ts 4382-4394, SQLite/libSQL, `isPostgres` false). No migration differ, no schema sync and no `os` command calls it: `packages/cli/src/utils/unmanaged-tables.ts:198-213` mirrors the listing statement and does not call the method (its PG mirror is unchanged); `schema-drift.ts` only references it in prose. The three internal `introspectColumns(tableName)` call sites (head 13854, 14178, 14638) pass no schema and keep their exact SQL.

Platform-owned callers: (a) the boot-time federated validation (`runtime/src/external-validation-plugin.ts`): a colliding federated datasource now rows EVERY object bound to it `unreachable` (validateEach 997-1025), and the plugin logs a warn and continues boot — no `onMismatch: 'fail'` abort for `unreachable` (326-349, the 2026-08-23 ruling). Coverage shrinks for that one datasource until the operator sets `schema`; before, its answer was wrong for the shadowed twin and the zero-column tables, so nothing correct is lost. (b) The platform's OWN datasource is built through the same factory (`default-datasource-driver-factory.ts:1146-1153` is the only `client: 'pg'` construction outside tests), but `listRemoteTables` refuses the primary outright, `testConnection` on the primary takes `checkHealth` whenever `liveDriver` is wired (plugin.ts 154-162 wires it), and no boot or sync path introspects it; a service constructed without `liveDriver` (tests, a bespoke host) would introspect the primary and answer `{ ok: false, error }` — the contract `testConnection` declares. (c) No per-tenant or per-organization schema switch exists in driver-sql: tenancy is a column (`organization_id`), `physicalSchemaByObject` is ADR-0015's per-object `external.remoteSchema` applied with `withSchema` on the builder (head 12255, 15610), not a `search_path`. An internal connection therefore sees two schemas only when the operator's role/database default `search_path` names them AND the datasource config carries no `schema`: `datasource-admin-service.ts:1061` judges the record with `DatasourceSchema.safeParse` but persists the RAW record, so a saved datasource that omits `schema` gets no knex `searchPath` and inherits the server default — exactly the card's measured shape, and the only platform door that can collide. A datasource with `schema` set (the spec default is `'public'`, postgres.zod.ts:247-250) has knex issue `set search_path to "one-schema"` per pooled connection and can never collide.

`testConnection` keeps its contract on both arms: the `catch` at 601-603 answers `{ ok: false, error: message }`; the admin plugin's `probe` answers `{ ok: false, error }` from its own catch (datasource-admin-plugin.ts 884-885).

**The detection — right.** Judged on `information_schema.tables` rows with `table_type = 'BASE TABLE'` and `table_schema = ANY (current_schemas(false))`, grouped by the stored `table_name`. Base tables only: views, foreign tables and materialized views are not rows and so never collide nor get listed — the same exclusions as before. Partitioned parents and partitions report `BASE TABLE` and are listed and counted exactly as before. Case folding and quoted identifiers: the stored name is compared, so `"Customers"` and `customers` are two keys, each read in its own schema — correct, because knex binds the same stored string in `columnInfo`. A schema not on the path (or not readable by the role) is excluded by `current_schemas(false)` — matching bare-name resolution, so nothing the connection cannot reach unqualified is refused. `current_schemas(false)` excludes the implicit `pg_catalog` / `pg_temp` entries, unchanged from `main`. Order: schemas per collision are sorted by `path_position`, collisions by name — deterministic text. Residual (the dev's own out-of-scope note, agreed): a VIEW in an earlier path schema named like a later schema's base table is not a collision; the base table is listed once with its own columns (the `withSchema` read), but `introspectPrimaryKeys`' `?::regclass` (head 21352) resolves the view and answers `primaryKeys: []`. `introspectForeignKeys` (`child.relname = ? AND ns.nspname = ANY (current_schemas(false))`, head 21163-21164) and `introspectUniqueConstraints` (`tc.table_schema = ANY (current_schemas(false))`, head 21524) merge rows of every same-named base table on the path, which the refusal now makes unambiguous among base tables; a view holds no constraints, so neither is disturbed by the shadow. Nothing the card names is missed.

**The column read — right, and the single-schema answer is unchanged by construction.** `introspectColumns(tableName, schema?)` (head 20987-20989) builds `this.knex(tableName)` and applies `.withSchema(schema)` only when a schema is passed; knex 3.3.0's pg compiler (`pg-querycompiler.js` 249-275, the version `pnpm-lock.yaml` pins; no knex is installed in this checkout, so read from the upstream source at that tag) then appends `and table_schema = ?` bound to the schema, else `and table_schema = current_schema()`. `introspectColumnOrder(tableName, schema?)` (head 20945-20958) mirrors it: `table_schema = ?` with `[tableName, schema]`, else `current_schema()` with `[tableName]` — byte-identical to `main` when `schema` is undefined, which is every caller except `introspectSchema`. For a single-schema connection, `schemaByTable.get(name)` is that one schema, so `table_schema = 'public'` replaces `current_schema()` with the same value; `columnInfo` output is keyed by column name and then ordered by `ORDER BY ordinal_position`, so columns, their order and types cannot differ; the three key reads are untouched, so `primaryKey` / `isUnique` flags and `primaryKeys` / `foreignKeys` cannot differ; the listing query adds two SELECT columns and no `ORDER BY`, so `tableNames` keeps the same row order as before (`rows.map` over `row.table_name`). The dev's claim of an identical sha256 (`a273d463…f8`, `introspectedAt` masked) is consistent with this reading; the code gives no path by which the single-schema answer could move.

**The refusal's text — right.** It names the count, the first colliding name with its schemas, the mechanism (one key, bare-name resolution to the first schema), every collision as `'table' ('schema1', 'schema2')` in `search_path` order, and two remedies: point the connection at one schema (the datasource's `schema` setting) or rename a table. The `schema` setting is real and read: declared at `packages/spec/src/data/driver/postgres.zod.ts:247-250` (`schema`, default `'public'`, described "Default schema (knex searchPath)"), consumed at `default-datasource-driver-factory.ts:1148-1153` as `cfg.schema → searchPath` on the `SqlDriver` config (`SqlDriverConfig = Knex.Config & {...}`, head 5198), which knex applies with `set search_path to "schema"` on every pooled connection. Setting it therefore yields a single-schema path and ends the collision. A deployment that needs tables from BOTH schemas is served by two datasources, one per schema; the text says "one schema per connection", which implies it without spelling it out — acceptable. Disclosure: the message names schema and table names the connection's own role can list; the HTTP callers are `manage_platform_settings` holders (admin-routes `requireDatasourceAdmin`) who can already list them through `listRemoteTables` and `?schema=`, and the existing `unattributedSchemaFilterError` already names tables the same way. No tracker number in the runtime string (AGENTS.md refusal-prose rule): correct; the `[#24707]` references are in code comments only.

Precision point, not a defect of this PR: at both HTTP doors a throw from `listRemoteTables` / `generateObjectDraft` / the saved-datasource test is answered `400 EXTERNAL_DATASOURCE_ERROR` carrying the message — `admin-routes.ts:635-641` (`badRequest`, 503 passthrough only) and `rest/external-datasource-routes.ts:459-470` (`answerThrown`: "Every other throw keeps this family's own 400 and code, a declared 4xx included"). The `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` pair is the driver's in-process contract (what `ObjectQL.introspectDatasource`, the service and `testConnection`'s `error` text see); the changeset's TO describes `introspectSchema()`'s throw and says the callers "surface that error", which they do by message. The PR's "answers the 409 through listRemoteTables" measurement was made on the service class with no server, as the body states. A CHANGELOG reader should not expect a 409 at the HTTP door; a one-line note in the changeset would remove the ambiguity. Not required for PASS: the HTTP mapping belongs to `service-datasource` / `rest`, outside this claim.

**The pins — assert the new truth with teeth; both ablation legs go red by construction.** `sql-driver-24707-introspect-pg-multischema.test.ts`, declared via `declareDialectCell(PG_CELL, …)` (testkit 506-540): without `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` it is `declareUnprovisionedCell` → a named skip, red under `OS_EXPECT_LIVE_DIALECT_MATRIX=1` (testkit 357-378). Fixture: the file's own isolated schema `here` (`currentLiveSchema()`, testkit 215-228) plus `here_b` (63-byte guard asserted), one driver with `searchPath: [here, there]` overriding the cell's single-schema `config()` (testkit 300-306), one control driver. Pin 1 (non-vacuity) asserts `current_schemas(false)` is exactly `[here, there]` and that the bare `columnInfo()` on the later schema's table answers `[]`. Pin 2 asserts the key set, the later table's exact 4-tuple column array `[name, type, primaryKey]`, its `primaryKeys`, and the first table's column names. Pin 3 creates the twin, asserts a throw is defined, `{ code: 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT', status: 409 }` exactly, and that the message contains `'os24707_customers' ('here', 'there')` — the named subjects. Pin 4 (control) asserts the single-schema key set, that `introspectColumns(name, here)` equals `introspectColumns(name)`, and the exact flag triples. Leg A (bare call in `introspectSchema`) makes pin 2's column array `[]` → red, as reported; leg B (refusal line deleted) makes `thrown` undefined → pin 3's `toBeDefined` red with exactly the reported "expected undefined to be defined". Imports `../src/index.js` like 115 sibling files in `src/`, so no dist leg; `tsconfig.json` includes `src/**/*`, so the file is type-checked (Type Check · workspace green).

What the lane means for THIS gate: `ci.yml:1693-1698` runs `temporal-conformance` only when `github.event_name` is neither `pull_request` nor `merge_group`, and its step "Run driver-sql suite against both live servers" (1825-1837) is where `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` and `OS_EXPECT_LIVE_DIALECT_MATRIX=1` are set. So on this head the check-run `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` is `skipped`, the Test Core shards ran the file as a named skip, and NO check-run on the head measured the four pins; the only measurement is the dev's local live run (4 passed; two red ablation legs), read as a claim. That is the standing shape of every live-PG pin in this package (the #11201 pin and the ~40 `declareDialectCell` files, ci.yml:349 "Temporal Conformance stay filtered exactly as they are today"): the live battery is main's push battery and a red there is a main-red the owning seat fixes. A pin that runs only after merge is acceptable here because it is the package's convention, not a deviation this PR introduces, and because the pins' SQL and assertions are plain enough to judge from the code — judged, and they hold.

### ② Semver level

**`minor` + BREAKING for `@objectstack/driver-sql` — right.** The accept set of `introspectSchema()` narrows on PostgreSQL (a connection that answered now throws), so `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the truthful arm (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs:95`: "NOT a widening, but breaking"), and `(narrowing)` is BREAKING (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3). The launch-window convention ships breaking as `minor` (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs:58-85`), with the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition as the mandatory carriers: both present. FROM (one of two tables answered), TO (`RESOURCE_CONFLICT` / 409, callers surface it), Fix (set `schema` or rename) are stated. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is at a line start in the changeset body (line 7) and in the PR body (line 3); `readClause2Line` (clause2-line.mjs 124, 226, 286) reads value `no` and arm `narrowing` from both. The ADR-0087 HTML-comment marker reads `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a `CATEGORIES` member (check-adr-0087-registration.mjs 147-154, refused only when the body prescribes rewriting consumer code — the Fix line prescribes connection configuration or a remote rename, not a code rewrite). Check Changeset and Lint · CI, release & engine gates are green on the head, so the gate's own reading agrees.

**The optional trailing `schema` parameter on two `protected` methods — a widened subclass-facing signature, not a new member, and not a Clause-② payload key; acceptable.** driver-sql emits declarations (`tsconfig.json` `declaration: true`, `package.json` `types: dist/index.d.ts`), and protected members appear in a published `.d.ts`, so `introspectColumns(tableName: string, schema?: string)` and `introspectColumnOrder(tableName: string, schema?: string)` are a visible change to every `SqlDriver` subclass. No gate reads driver-sql's surface (`packages/spec/api-surface/*.json` cover spec entries only). In-tree subclasses: `TursoDriver` overrides `introspectColumns(tableName: string)` with the old arity (turso-driver.ts:4014) — assignable, compiles (Type Check · workspace green), and behaviourally right because on SQLite/libSQL `introspectSchema` always passes `undefined`; `SqliteWasmDriver` overrides neither; the in-package `LegacyStorageDriver` testkit overrides neither. An out-of-tree PostgreSQL subclass that overrides `introspectColumns` with the old arity would drop the schema and keep `main`'s bare read — no regression against `main`. It is not a "new public member on an exported class": no member is added, both are `protected`, and the helper `postgresTableNameCollisionError` is module-private. A private helper could carry the fix with no signature change (read `schemaByTable` inside `introspectSchema` and call a private schema-scoped reader), but it would hide the schema from the one seam a subclass demonstrably overrides (`TursoDriver` does), so the chosen shape is the sounder one. The changeset does not mention the new parameter; the PR body does. Additive and optional, so no FROM/TO is owed for it; a sentence for subclass authors would be an improvement, not a requirement.

**Nothing else widens.** No new export (`git diff`: the only new top-level declaration is the un-exported helper), no new error code (`RESOURCE_CONFLICT` exists in `errors.zod.ts:95` with standard status 409 at `errors.zod.ts:189`), no spec key, no `IntrospectedTable` member, no `packages/spec` path in the file list.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Pins' CI lane** — answered in ①: not measured by any check-run on this head; standing convention of the package; acceptable, named here so the post-merge battery's first run on `main` is read as the measurement of record.
- **Consumer name** — the dispatch's `service-external-datasource` is `@objectstack/service-datasource` at `packages/services/service-datasource` (`ExternalDatasourceService` in `external-datasource-service.ts`); the PR's file list has no path under it. Confirmed, nothing there edited.
- **#11201 and #24664 read through the in-tree record** — acceptable: the FK arm's docblock (head 21110-21116, "Scoping is unchanged in meaning (#11201)") and the `sql-driver-11201-introspect-fk-schema-scope.test.ts` header carry #11201's ruling; `unattributedSchemaFilterError` (external-datasource-service.ts 250-307) carries #24664's. I read #11201's thread myself: the fix shape (`current_schemas(false)` pin) and the collision shape (same-named table in a sibling schema) match the in-tree record. Same-shape precedent for this card's reads.
- **Throwaway PostgreSQL directory at `/tmp/os-issue-24707-pg`** — a claim (nothing in the diff can show it); the stated reason (the scratchpad parent is mode 700, which the `postgres` user cannot enter) is plausible, and the repo-cleanliness rule (Checklist 7) is met by the diff: three intended files, nothing else. Noted as unverifiable from here.
- **Five pushes to one branch** — the branch holds four commits (fix, test, changeset, merge of `origin/main`); five pushes with an initial empty push match "push before every step that takes minutes". Not a breach.
- **Commit trailers** — the three authored commits carry `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013timUNNCthRfQkhy9Hz2fV` and a `Co-authored-by` line naming no product version; the merge commit carries none. Conforms to the repo's trailer rule (AGENTS.md attribution outranks the harness reminder).
